title: Education & Class: Policy & Marketisation
welcome_lead: From comprehensives to academies — policy shapes the class gap.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology education policy 1944 Tripartite 1988 Education Reform Act marketisation.
final_note: Each reform claims to widen access; outcomes vary.

walkthroughs.body_html: The 1944 Education Act created tripartite system: grammar (top 20%), technical, secondary modern. The 11-plus sorted children. 1965 Labour Circular 10/65 pushed comprehensives — by 1980s most state schools comprehensive. Grammar schools survive in some LAs (e.g. Kent).

1988 ERA (Conservative): National Curriculum, SATs, league tables, open enrolment, formula funding, LMS. Marketisation — schools compete for pupils whose families bring funding. Bartlett (1993): schools cream-skim, silt-shift, and select high-attainers.

2000 onwards Labour academies replaced failing schools. Coalition (2010) expanded academies and added free schools (Sweden model). Ball (2003): parentocracy — middle-class parents better informed, gaining best schools. EBacc and Pupil Premium try to address gaps.
